title: FEW x Credit Suisse Panel Discussion | The Journey of Female Entrepreneurs
description: The FEW x Credit Suisse Panel discussion - The Journey of Female Entrepreneurs on May 11th was a tremendous success. We invited three talented entrepreneurs two of whom are also investors, Donna Nguyen-Phuoc and Katherine Lui, plus a new generation entrepreneur, Jen Loong to share their stories including their entrepreneurial journey. We were also honoured to have the chairman of Credit Suisse Hong Kong, Carsten Stoehr to moderate the panel and he discussed with us how men can support women for success.

asr.full_text: Today will be an interesting and insightful session. I'm delighted to be here on stage with three tremendous entrepreneurs. When I was back in as a kid, I always have one philosophy in mind. Whatever you do, be happy. That ingredients has to exist first, that you are always very optimistic about the outcome of what you're trying to do. Because as an entrepreneur, you never know whether you will succeed or you will fail. People say you cannot do it, but in fact we could do it. FIONA HAN CHUNHANANHUWIN HABUKU HENG GONGTANGAWA AYI It was all about recognising a market opportunity. So when I was in second year in university, I was back in Saigon and I was working as a summer job for a UK company and then I saw there was a market opportunity, there was a lot of demand for technology. I started my first company, a trading company, opened the company became their distributor. Follow the demand! there has to be a demand for you to go and supply something Entrepreneurs are renaissance men and women, I think we are highly ADHD anything that's new that almost is a frontier that you want to learn about your deeply curious you see an opportunity and I grew up in that type of household, as an entrepreneur you have to care deeply about the impact that you'll have in whatever thesis that you're trying to prove. You didn't mention one thing I thought you would mention which is your focus on the gender equality. Now of course we live in a very sensitive environment the gendered is constantly spoken. So I'll actually advocate the other side that were entrepreneurs first gender after that. It's difficult enough to be an entrepreneur is there a difference from your perspective of being a female entrepreneur? It is the difference but I think it's an advantage. When you walk into a conference or a room that's always like 95 male and five female so they remember you. Tell us about how has an advocate or mentor played an important role to enable you to be who you are today? Because of my role as an acting CFO I see a lot of entrepreneurs, a lot of successful businessmen trying to improve or grow their business. They always will inspire me. I actually learn by consulting them. As a woman you have special traits. Have you in your experience at any time brought to fore and saw that you could use those traits? I think as a female in general you have higher EQ do you listen more and if you sit in front of male, usually they tend to talk to you more because there's no ego. There's no competition. A deep power that women have, and in fact men should also harness, is just this idea of empathy, being able to relate to others to really bond and be compassionate from a point of where they're starting from rather than what they're doing, or what they're actually showing us. I have a lot of good friends and we are like a soldiers, a group of people working towards a goal. I never really remember who I am from the gender's point of view. What do you do as a company or as the CEO of a company? Not only empower, power but to support the female colleagues that you have? What is the tone that we set? And how do we operate? Making sure that that framework is very clear and is engaging and is enabling talent to surface, irrespective of gender, is very, very important.

The visual evidence shows a moderated stage conversation, while references to investors are presented as part of their stories rather than as a financial offer or participation flow. A general disclaimer appears at the end, and the described material does not show a solicitation or deceptive investment promise.
